POLICY DOMAIN: device

[Dates and evidence]
Elapsed days are calendar date differences, with the start date counted as zero. Weekends are included. Use incident minus inception for the waiting interval and report minus incident for notice. A repair appointment or an earlier estimate is not the report date. The claim facts below are accepted findings, not allegations requiring further proof. A listed accepted exception is valid for this incident and the specified cover. A not-accepted exception supplies no waiver.

[Cover C3] console failure
This cover responds only to console failure. Its whole-item category is game console. Its named-item category is controller; a loss to that named item belongs to this cover even when it is an attachment to a larger item. Benefit ceiling: $6500.00. One deductible: $90.00. Named-item sublimit: $480.00. The sublimit applies only to controller; all other items in this cover use only the benefit ceiling. Waiting interval: 10 elapsed days from inception. An incident on the final waiting boundary is eligible. Notice interval: 21 elapsed days from incident to report, inclusive. Threshold exclusion: device age in months greater than 54. Exception: extended-service endorsement accepted for this cover removes only that threshold exclusion. Flag exclusion: unapproved repair facility. This means the repair was performed by a facility outside the approved list. Exception: written alternate-facility authorization accepted for this cover removes only that flag exclusion. An exception to one exclusion does not waive another exclusion, a waiting period, a notice deadline or purchase status. The event, item and incident must all belong to the same cover; another section cannot supply a higher limit or a smaller deductible. Costs for a whole item and its named component are alternative descriptions of the same loss and cannot be added together. The approved loss in the claim file is already adjusted for salvage, depreciation, taxes and any recoveries. These adjustments must not be deducted a second time.

[Common exclusions and order]
An intentionally caused loss is excluded and has no exception. If more than one denial applies, use this priority: not purchased; waiting interval; late notice; threshold exclusion; flag exclusion; intentional loss. If no denial applies, settle the amount using the calculation section. All rules governing this fictional claim are stated here; no outside customary exclusions or unstated document requirements apply.

[Allocation of the claim]
Only the single event and item named in the claim file are being claimed. Other covers remain in the booklet so the reader can distinguish similar but inapplicable benefits. Their purchase status, waiting intervals, exclusions and limits do not alter this claim. A reference to a part in another section does not reclassify the item in this file. The claimed amount contains no unrelated fees, future losses or duplicate invoices. There is no currency conversion and all amounts are US dollars.

[Settlement calculation]
Subtract one deductible from approved loss, flooring at zero, then cap the remainder by the applicable ceilings. The applicable ceiling is the lesser of the benefit ceiling and any named-item sublimit. For whole-item claims there is no named-item ceiling. A ceiling binds only when it is strictly below the amount entering the cap operation; equality is not a binding ceiling. When no ceiling binds, use the loss-based settlement description. If both ceilings are present, the smaller ceiling supplies the settlement description. Pay once per incident; there is no stacking or extra deductible from another cover.
